sanskrit: tatas tāṃś codayām āsa vāyuvegasamāñ jave yena tat tripuraṃ rājan daityadānavarakṣitam
english: Then, O king, he urged on those steeds, swift as the rushing wind, toward that Tripura which was guarded by the Daityas and Dānavas.

sanskrit: athādhijyaṃ dhanuḥ kṛtvā śarvaḥ saṃdhāya taṃ śaram yuktvā pāśupatāstreṇa tripuraṃ samacintayat
english: Then Śarva, having strung his bow and fitted that arrow to it, joined it with the Pāśupata weapon and fixed his thought upon Tripura.

sanskrit: tasmin sthite tadā rājan kruddhe vidhṛtakārmuke purāṇi tāni kālena jagmur ekatvatāṃ tadā
english: While he stood thus, O king, wrathful and with bow upraised, those three cities at that very moment, through the working of Time, became one.

sanskrit: ekībhāvaṃ gate caiva tripure samupāgate babhūva tumulo harṣo daivatānāṃ mahātmanām
english: And when the three cities had thus merged into one and come together, a tumultuous joy arose among the high-souled gods.

sanskrit: tato devagaṇāḥ sarve siddhāś ca paramarṣayaḥ jayeti vāco mumucuḥ saṃstuvanto mudānvitāḥ
english: Then all the hosts of gods, the Siddhas, and the supreme sages, filled with gladness and singing his praises, sent up the cry of "Victory!"

sanskrit: tato 'grataḥ prādurabhūt tripuraṃ jaghnuṣo 'surān anirdeśyogravapuṣo devasyāsahyatejasaḥ
english: Then before that god — of form too terrible to describe and of unbearable splendor — who was about to slay the Asuras, Tripura came into view.

sanskrit: sa tad vikṛṣya bhagavān divyaṃ lokeśvaro dhanuḥ trailokyasāraṃ tam iṣuṃ mumoca tripuraṃ prati tat sāsuragaṇaṃ dagdhvā prākṣipat paścimārṇave
english: Drawing that divine bow, the blessed Lord of the worlds loosed against Tripura that arrow which held the essence of the three worlds; and having burned that city together with its hosts of Asuras, he hurled it into the western ocean.

sanskrit: evaṃ tat tripuraṃ dagdhaṃ dānavāś cāpy aśeṣataḥ maheśvareṇa kruddhena trailokyasya hitaiṣiṇā
english: Thus was Tripura burned, and the Dānavas too without remainder, by the wrathful Maheśvara, who sought the welfare of the three worlds.

sanskrit: sa cātmakrodhajo vahnir hāhety uktvā nivāritaḥ mā kārṣīr bhasmasāl lokān iti tryakṣo 'bravīc ca tam
english: And that fire, born of his own wrath, crying "Alas! Alas!", was checked; for the three-eyed god said to it, "Do not reduce the worlds to ashes."

sanskrit: tataḥ prakṛtim āpannā devā lokās tatharṣayaḥ tuṣṭuvur vāgbhir arthyābhiḥ sthāṇum apratimaujasam
english: Then the gods, the worlds, and the sages, restored to their natural state, praised Sthāṇu of incomparable might with words rich in meaning.

sanskrit: te 'nujñātā bhagavatā jagmuḥ sarve yathāgatam kṛtakāmāḥ prasannena prajāpatimukhāḥ surāḥ
english: Dismissed by the blessed Lord, all the gods, their desires fulfilled, departed as they had come, with Prajāpati at their head and gladdened in heart.

sanskrit: yathaiva bhagavān brahmā lokadhātā pitāmahaḥ saṃyaccha tvaṃ hayān asya rādheyasya mahātmanaḥ
english: Even as the blessed Brahmā, the Grandsire and sustainer of the worlds, once held the reins, so do you govern the steeds of this high-souled son of Rādhā.

sanskrit: tvaṃ hi kṛṣṇāc ca karṇāc ca phalgunāc ca viśeṣataḥ viśiṣṭo rājaśārdūla nāsti tatra vicāraṇā
english: For you, O tiger among kings, are superior to Kṛṣṇa, to Karṇa, and above all to Phalguna; in this there is no doubt.

sanskrit: yuddhe hy ayaṃ rudrakalpas tvaṃ ca brahmasamo 'nagha tasmāc chaktau yuvāṃ jetuṃ macchatrūṃs tāv ivāsurān
english: For in battle this one is the equal of Rudra, and you, O sinless one, are the equal of Brahmā; therefore the two of you are able to vanquish my foes, as those two vanquished the Asuras.

sanskrit: yathā śalyādya karṇo 'yaṃ śvetāśvaṃ kṛṣṇasārathim pramathya hanyāt kaunteyaṃ tathā śīghraṃ vidhīyatām tvayi karṇaś ca rājyaṃ ca vayaṃ caiva pratiṣṭhitāḥ
english: O Śalya, contrive it swiftly today that this Karṇa may crush and slay the son of Kuntī, him of the white steeds and Kṛṣṇa as charioteer; for upon you rest Karṇa, the kingdom, and we ourselves.

sanskrit: imaṃ cāpy aparaṃ bhūya itihāsaṃ nibodha me pitur mama sakāśe yaṃ brāhmaṇaḥ prāha dharmavit
english: And hear from me yet this other ancient tale besides, which a brāhmaṇa learned in dharma told in the presence of my father.

sanskrit: śrutvā caitad vacaś citraṃ hetukāryārthasaṃhitam kuru śalya viniścitya mā bhūd atra vicāraṇā
english: And having heard this wondrous speech, fraught with cause, effect, and meaning, do you act, O Śalya, with firm resolve; let there be no hesitation in this.

sanskrit: bhārgavāṇāṃ kule jāto jamadagnir mahātapāḥ tasya rāmeti vikhyātaḥ putras tejoguṇānvitaḥ
english: Born in the lineage of the Bhārgavas was Jamadagni, of great austerities; his son, famed as Rāma, was endowed with splendor and excellence.

sanskrit: sa tīvraṃ tapa āsthāya prasādayitavān bhavam astrahetoḥ prasannātmā niyataḥ saṃyatendriyaḥ
english: Undertaking fierce austerities, serene of soul, self-disciplined, and with senses restrained, he won the favor of Bhava for the sake of celestial weapons.

sanskrit: tasya tuṣṭo mahādevo bhaktyā ca praśamena ca hṛdgataṃ cāsya vijñāya darśayām āsa śaṃkaraḥ
english: Pleased with him for his devotion and his tranquility, and knowing what lay in his heart, Mahādeva — Śaṃkara — showed himself to him.

sanskrit: īśvara uvāca rāma tuṣṭo 'smi bhadraṃ te viditaṃ me tavepsitam kuruṣva pūtam ātmānaṃ sarvam etad avāpsyasi
english: The Lord said: Rāma, I am pleased with you; blessings upon you. Known to me is your desire. Make yourself pure, and all this you shall obtain.

sanskrit: dāsyāmi te tadāstrāṇi yadā pūto bhaviṣyasi apātram asamarthaṃ ca dahanty astrāṇi bhārgava
english: I shall give you those weapons when you have become pure; for the weapons consume, O Bhārgava, one who is unworthy and incapable.

sanskrit: ity ukto jāmadagnyas tu devadevena śūlinā pratyuvāca mahātmānaṃ śirasāvanataḥ prabhum
english: Thus addressed by the trident-bearing God of gods, the son of Jamadagni, bowing his head, replied to the high-souled Lord.

sanskrit: yadā jānāsi deveśa pātraṃ mām astradhāraṇe tadā śuśrūṣate 'strāṇi bhavān me dātum arhati
english: When you know me, O Lord of the gods, to be worthy of bearing the weapons, then upon me, who serve you faithfully, it will be fitting that you bestow them.

sanskrit: duryodhana uvāca tataḥ sa tapasā caiva damena niyamena ca pūjopahārabalibhir homamantrapuraskṛtaiḥ
english: Duryodhana said: Then, through austerity, self-mastery, and observance, with worship, offerings, and oblations attended by sacrificial fires and sacred chants,

sanskrit: ārādhayitavāñ śarvaṃ bahūn varṣagaṇāṃs tadā prasannaś ca mahādevo bhārgavasya mahātmanaḥ
english: he propitiated Śarva for many long years; and Mahādeva became gracious toward the high-souled Bhārgava.

sanskrit: abravīt tasya bahuśo guṇān devyāḥ samīpataḥ bhaktimān eṣa satataṃ mayi rāmo dṛḍhavrataḥ
english: Again and again he spoke of his virtues in the presence of the Goddess: "This Rāma, firm in his vows, is ever devoted to me."

sanskrit: evaṃ tasya guṇān prīto bahuśo 'kathayat prabhuḥ devatānāṃ pitṝṇāṃ ca samakṣam arisūdanaḥ
english: Thus did the gracious Lord, the slayer of foes, recount his virtues many times in the presence of the gods and the ancestral fathers.

sanskrit: etasminn eva kāle tu daityā āsan mahābalāḥ tais tadā darpamohāndhair abādhyanta divaukasaḥ
english: Now at that very time there were Daityas of mighty strength, and by them, blinded with pride and delusion, the dwellers of heaven were oppressed.

sanskrit: tataḥ saṃbhūya vibudhās tān hantuṃ kṛtaniścayāḥ cakruḥ śatruvadhe yatnaṃ na śekur jetum eva te
english: Then the gods, banded together and resolved to slay them, made every effort to destroy the foe, yet were unable to conquer them.

sanskrit: abhigamya tato devā maheśvaram athābruvan prasādayantas taṃ bhaktyā jahi śatrugaṇān iti
english: Then the gods, approaching Maheśvara and propitiating him with devotion, said to him, "Slay the hosts of our enemies."

sanskrit: pratijñāya tato devo devatānāṃ ripukṣayam rāmaṃ bhārgavam āhūya so 'bhyabhāṣata śaṃkaraḥ
english: Then the god, having promised the gods the destruction of their foes, summoned Rāma the Bhārgava, and Śaṃkara spoke to him.

sanskrit: ripūn bhārgava devānāṃ jahi sarvān samāgatān lokānāṃ hitakāmārthaṃ matprītyarthaṃ tathaiva ca
english: O Bhārgava, slay all the gathered enemies of the gods, for the welfare of the worlds, and likewise for my own pleasure.

sanskrit: rāma uvāca akṛtāstrasya deveśa kā śaktir me maheśvara nihantuṃ dānavān sarvān kṛtāstrān yuddhadurmadān
english: Rāma said: O Lord of the gods, O Maheśvara, what power have I, untrained in arms, to slay all these Dānavas, skilled in arms and frenzied in battle?

sanskrit: īśvara uvāca gaccha tvaṃ madanudhyānān nihaniṣyasi dānavān vijitya ca ripūn sarvān guṇān prāpsyasi puṣkalān
english: The Lord said: Go; by meditating upon me you shall slay the Dānavas, and having conquered all your foes you shall attain abundant excellences.

sanskrit: duryodhana uvāca etac chrutvā ca vacanaṃ pratigṛhya ca sarvaśaḥ rāmaḥ kṛtasvastyayanaḥ prayayau dānavān prati
english: Duryodhana said: And having heard this speech and wholly accepted it, Rāma, when the rites of benediction had been performed, set forth against the Dānavas.

sanskrit: avadhīd devaśatrūṃs tān madadarpabalānvitān vajrāśanisamasparśaiḥ prahārair eva bhārgavaḥ
english: And the Bhārgava slew those enemies of the gods, filled with frenzy, pride, and strength, with blows whose touch was like the thunderbolt and the lightning.

sanskrit: sa dānavaiḥ kṣatatanur jāmadagnyo dvijottamaḥ saṃspṛṣṭaḥ sthāṇunā sadyo nirvraṇaḥ samajāyata
english: Though his body was wounded by the Dānavas, that foremost of the twice-born, the son of Jamadagni, when touched by Sthāṇu became at once free of wounds.

sanskrit: prītaś ca bhagavān devaḥ karmaṇā tena tasya vai varān prādād brahmavide bhārgavāya mahātmane
english: And the blessed god, pleased with that deed of his, granted boons to the high-souled Bhārgava, knower of the Veda.

sanskrit: uktaś ca devadevena prītiyuktena śūlinā nipātāt tava śastrāṇāṃ śarīre yābhavad rujā
english: And by the trident-bearing God of gods, filled with affection, he was told: "The pain that arose in your body from the fall of the foes' weapons —

sanskrit: tayā te mānuṣaṃ karma vyapoḍhaṃ bhṛgunandana gṛhāṇāstrāṇi divyāni matsakāśād yathepsitam
english: by that pain your human deed has been wiped away, O delight of the Bhṛgus. Receive now from me the celestial weapons, as you desire."

sanskrit: tato 'strāṇi samastāni varāṃś ca manasepsitān labdhvā bahuvidhān rāmaḥ praṇamya śirasā śivam
english: Then, having received all the weapons and the manifold boons his mind had longed for, Rāma bowed his head to Śiva.

sanskrit: anujñāṃ prāpya deveśāj jagāma sa mahātapāḥ evam etat purāvṛttaṃ tadā kathitavān ṛṣiḥ
english: And having obtained leave of the Lord of the gods, that great ascetic departed. Thus did the sage recount this event of olden time.

sanskrit: bhārgavo 'py adadāt sarvaṃ dhanurvedaṃ mahātmane karṇāya puruṣavyāghra suprītenāntarātmanā
english: And the Bhārgava too, O tiger among men, with inmost soul well pleased, imparted the whole science of archery to the high-souled Karṇa.

sanskrit: vṛjinaṃ hi bhavet kiṃ cid yadi karṇasya pārthiva nāsmai hy astrāṇi divyāni prādāsyad bhṛgunandanaḥ
english: For had there been any taint in Karṇa, O king, the delight of the Bhṛgus would never have given him the celestial weapons.

sanskrit: nāpi sūtakule jātaṃ karṇaṃ manye kathaṃ cana devaputram ahaṃ manye kṣatriyāṇāṃ kulodbhavam
english: Nor do I in any wise believe Karṇa to be born in the lineage of a charioteer; I deem him the son of a god, sprung from the race of the Kṣatriyas.

sanskrit: sakuṇḍalaṃ sakavacaṃ dīrghabāhuṃ mahāratham katham ādityasadṛśaṃ mṛgī vyāghraṃ janiṣyati
english: How should a doe bring forth a tiger — this long-armed great warrior, like the sun, with his earrings and his armor?

sanskrit: paśya hy asya bhujau pīnau nāgarājakaropamau vakṣaḥ paśya viśālaṃ ca sarvaśatrunibarhaṇam
english: Behold his arms, brawny and like the trunks of the king of elephants; behold his broad chest, the crusher of all foes.

sanskrit: duryodhana uvāca evaṃ sa bhagavān devaḥ sarvalokapitāmahaḥ sārathyam akarot tatra yatra rudro 'bhavad rathī
english: Duryodhana said: Thus did that blessed god, the Grandsire of all the worlds, perform the office of charioteer there where Rudra rode upon the car.

sanskrit: rathinābhyadhiko vīraḥ kartavyo rathasārathiḥ tasmāt tvaṃ puruṣavyāghra niyaccha turagān yudhi
english: A chariot's charioteer should be a hero greater than the warrior himself; therefore, O tiger among men, do you govern the steeds in battle.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca tataḥ śalyaḥ pariṣvajya sutaṃ te vākyam abravīt duryodhanam amitraghnaḥ prīto madrādhipas tadā
english: Saṃjaya said: Then Śalya, lord of the Madras, slayer of foes, embracing your son Duryodhana and well pleased, spoke these words.

sanskrit: evaṃ cen manyase rājan gāndhāre priyadarśana tasmāt te yat priyaṃ kiṃ cit tat sarvaṃ karavāṇy aham
english: If, O king, you so judge it, O son of Gāndhārī, fair to behold, then whatever is dear to you, all that I shall do.

sanskrit: yatrāsmi bharataśreṣṭha yogyaḥ karmaṇi karhi cit tatra sarvātmanā yukto vakṣye kāryadhuraṃ tava
english: O best of the Bharatas, in whatsoever task I am at any time fit, there, devoting myself wholly to it, I shall take up the burden of your work.

sanskrit: yat tu karṇam ahaṃ brūyāṃ hitakāmaḥ priyāpriyam mama tatkṣamatāṃ sarvaṃ bhavān karṇaś ca sarvaśaḥ
english: But whatever I, seeking his good, may say to Karṇa, be it pleasant or unpleasant — let your honor and Karṇa pardon me all of it utterly.

sanskrit: karṇa uvāca īśānasya yathā brahmā yathā pārthasya keśavaḥ tathā nityaṃ hite yukto madrarāja bhajasva naḥ
english: Karṇa said: As Brahmā is ever devoted to the good of Īśāna, and Keśava to the good of Pārtha, so, O king of the Madras, be devoted always to ours.

sanskrit: śalya uvāca ātmanindātmapūjā ca paranindā parastavaḥ anācaritam āryāṇāṃ vṛttam etac caturvidham
english: Śalya said: Self-reproach and self-praise, the censure of others and the flattery of others — this fourfold conduct is not practiced by the noble.

sanskrit: yat tu vidvan pravakṣyāmi pratyayārtham ahaṃ tava ātmanaḥ stavasaṃyuktaṃ tan nibodha yathātatham
english: Yet what I shall now declare, O learned one, for the sake of your assurance — though it be joined with praise of myself — hear it truly as it is.

sanskrit: ahaṃ śakrasya sārathye yogyo mātalivat prabho apramādaprayogāc ca jñānavidyācikitsitaiḥ
english: I am fit to drive the chariot of Śakra, even as Mātali, O lord, through unfailing skill and through my knowledge, learning, and remedies.

sanskrit: tataḥ pārthena saṃgrāme yudhyamānasya te 'nagha vāhayiṣyāmi turagān vijvaro bhava sūtaja
english: Therefore, O sinless one, while you fight with Pārtha in the battle, I shall drive your steeds; be free of fever, O son of the charioteer.

sanskrit: duryodhana uvāca ayaṃ te karṇa sārathyaṃ madrarājaḥ kariṣyati kṛṣṇād abhyadhiko yantā devendrasyeva mātaliḥ
english: Duryodhana said: This king of the Madras, O Karṇa, will be your charioteer, a driver greater than Kṛṣṇa, even as Mātali is to the lord of the gods.

sanskrit: yathā harihayair yuktaṃ saṃgṛhṇāti sa mātaliḥ śalyas tava tathādyāyaṃ saṃyantā rathavājinām
english: As Mātali guides the chariot yoked with tawny steeds, so today shall this Śalya be the controller of your chariot-horses.

sanskrit: yodhe tvayi rathasthe ca madrarāje ca sārathau rathaśreṣṭho dhruvaṃ saṃkhye pārtho nābhibhaviṣyati
english: With you the warrior upon the car and the king of the Madras as charioteer, surely in battle Pārtha, foremost of car-warriors, shall not prevail.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca tato duryodhano bhūyo madrarājaṃ tarasvinam uvāca rājan saṃgrāme saṃyacchantaṃ hayottamān
english: Saṃjaya said: Then, O king, Duryodhana spoke once more to the impetuous king of the Madras, who was to govern the noble steeds in battle.

sanskrit: tvayābhigupto rādheyo vijeṣyati dhanaṃjayam ity ukto ratham āsthāya tatheti prāha bhārata
english: "Guarded by you, the son of Rādhā shall conquer Dhanaṃjaya." Thus addressed, O Bhārata, Śalya mounted the chariot and said, "So be it."

sanskrit: śalye 'bhyupagate karṇaḥ sārathiṃ sumano 'bravīt svaṃ sūta syandanaṃ mahyaṃ kalpayety asakṛt tvaran
english: When Śalya had consented, Karṇa, glad of heart, said to his charioteer again and again, hastening him: "Charioteer, make ready my car for me."

sanskrit: tato jaitraṃ rathavaraṃ gandharvanagaropamam vidhivat kalpitaṃ bhartre jayety uktvā nyavedayat
english: Then, having duly made ready that victorious and excellent chariot, like a city of the Gandharvas, he presented it to his master, saying, "Victory!"

sanskrit: taṃ rathaṃ rathināṃ śreṣṭhaḥ karṇo 'bhyarcya yathāvidhi saṃpāditaṃ brahmavidā pūrvam eva purodhasā
english: That chariot, which the household priest, knower of the Veda, had earlier consecrated, Karṇa, foremost of car-warriors, worshipped according to rule.

sanskrit: kṛtvā pradakṣiṇaṃ yatnād upasthāya ca bhāskaram samīpasthaṃ madrarājaṃ samāropayad agrataḥ
english: Reverently circling it and worshipping the Sun, he had the king of the Madras, who stood beside him, mount up in front.

sanskrit: tataḥ karṇasya durdharṣaṃ syandanapravaraṃ mahat āruroha mahātejāḥ śalyaḥ siṃha ivācalam
english: Then the mighty-splendored Śalya ascended Karṇa's great and unassailable chariot, foremost of cars, as a lion ascends a mountain.

sanskrit: tataḥ śalyāsthitaṃ rājan karṇaḥ svaratham uttamam adhyatiṣṭhad yathāmbhodaṃ vidyutvantaṃ divākaraḥ
english: Then, O king, Karṇa mounted his own excellent chariot, on which Śalya was already stationed, as the sun mounts a lightning-bearing cloud.

sanskrit: tāv ekaratham ārūḍhāv ādityāgnisamatviṣau vyabhrājetāṃ yathā meghaṃ sūryāgnī sahitau divi
english: Mounted upon one chariot, those two, in splendor like the sun and fire, shone forth as the sun and fire together blaze upon a cloud in the sky.

sanskrit: saṃstūyamānau tau vīrau tadāstāṃ dyutimattarau ṛtvik sadasyair indrāgnī hūyamānāv ivādhvare
english: Those two heroes, hymned in praise, shone then with surpassing radiance, like Indra and Agni invoked by priest and assembled celebrants at a sacrifice.

sanskrit: sa śalyasaṃgṛhītāśve rathe karṇaḥ sthito 'bhavat dhanur visphārayan ghoraṃ pariveṣīva bhāskaraḥ
english: There stood Karṇa upon the chariot whose steeds Śalya held, twanging his dreadful bow, like the sun girt round with a halo.

sanskrit: āsthitaḥ sa rathaśreṣṭhaṃ karṇaḥ śaragabhastimān prababhau puruṣavyāghro mandarastha ivāṃśumān
english: Stationed upon that foremost of chariots, Karṇa, that tiger among men, his arrows for his rays, shone like the radiant sun resting upon Mount Mandara.

sanskrit: taṃ rathasthaṃ mahāvīraṃ yāntaṃ cāmitatejasam duryodhanaḥ sma rādheyam idaṃ vacanam abravīt
english: To that great hero of measureless splendor, the son of Rādhā, as he stood upon the car and went forth, Duryodhana spoke these words.

sanskrit: akṛtaṃ droṇabhīṣmābhyāṃ duṣkaraṃ karma saṃyuge kuruṣvādhirathe vīra miṣatāṃ sarvadhanvinām
english: That hard deed in battle which Droṇa and Bhīṣma left undone, accomplish it, O hero, son of Adhiratha, before the eyes of all the bowmen.

sanskrit: manogataṃ mama hy āsīd bhīṣmadroṇau mahārathau arjunaṃ bhīmasenaṃ ca nihantārāv iti dhruvam
english: For it was my settled hope that the two great car-warriors Bhīṣma and Droṇa would surely slay Arjuna and Bhīmasena.

sanskrit: tābhyāṃ yad akṛtaṃ vīra vīrakarma mahāmṛdhe tat karma kuru rādheya vajrapāṇir ivāparaḥ
english: That heroic deed which the two of them left undone in the great battle, do you accomplish it, O son of Rādhā, like a second Wielder of the Thunderbolt.

sanskrit: gṛhāṇa dharmarājaṃ vā jahi vā tvaṃ dhanaṃjayam bhīmasenaṃ ca rādheya mādrīputrau yamāv api
english: Either take captive the King of Dharma, or slay Dhanaṃjaya, and Bhīmasena too, O son of Rādhā, and the twin sons of Mādrī.

sanskrit: jayaś ca te 'stu bhadraṃ ca prayāhi puruṣarṣabha pāṇḍuputrasya sainyāni kuru sarvāṇi bhasmasāt
english: Victory be yours, and blessings upon you. Go forth, O bull among men, and reduce all the armies of the son of Pāṇḍu to ashes.
